posting.title: Building Performance Specialist
posting.description:
KieranTimberlake is seeking a Building Performance Specialist to join our Philadelphia studio. Our projects span civic, academic, cultural, and institutional work, and you’ll work alongside colleagues who engage deeply across all phases, from early design through construction administration, and who are invested equally in design excellence and environmental performance.


Founded in 1984, KieranTimberlake unites the expertise and talents of professionals from diverse backgrounds in a practice that is recognized globally. In 2025, after 40 years as a founder-led firm, we transitioned to 100% employee ownership, a milestone that reflects a deep commitment to our staff.

Your Role

The Building Performance Specialist will be a member of KieranTimberlake’s Research Group and will work to advance sustainable, high-performing building design across the practice. They will be responsible for applying their experience in building performance analysis and sustainable design to advise project teams, advocate with clients, and guide consultants and colleagues toward measurable environmental outcomes. While the role includes hands-on energy, carbon, daylight, and comfort modeling, its emphasis is strategic: setting performance targets, shaping design decisions, and translating analysis into design direction. Working with Design Computation researchers, they will co-develop digital workflows that automate analysis and make performance methods accessible to peers.

What you’ll do:

  1. Advance office-wide performance literacy and sustainable design ambition
  2. Advise project teams on performance strategies across all project phases
  3. Collaborate closely with architects so performance thinking shapes design from the start
  4. Advocate to clients for ambitious, evidence-based sustainability goals
  5. Guide consultants and colleagues toward integrated, high-performing designs
  6. Execute energy, carbon, daylight, and comfort modeling to inform early design
  7. Translate analysis into clear visual feedback that supports an iterative design process
  8. Steward performance targets, benchmarking, and reporting across projects
  9. Co-develop automated analysis workflows with Design Computation peers
  10. Evaluate emerging simulation tools, certification frameworks, and regulations
  11. Lead office-wide sustainability initiatives with Research Group colleagues
  12. Engage in interdisciplinary brainstorming sessions across a wide range of topics, including building performance, environmental justice, human health, post-occupancy evaluation, and many others

Your Qualifications

The ideal candidate is a thoughtful, curious individual who wants to be part of a collaborative, interdisciplinary team and can demonstrate:

  1. A degree in architecture, engineering, or other design- or building science-related field
  2. At least 5 years of experience in building performance analysis and sustainable design
  3. Expertise in energy, daylight, thermal comfort, and embodied carbon modeling
  4. Experience guiding projects through performance and certification frameworks
  5. Experience working collaboratively within architectural design teams
  6. Sensitivity to the pace and realities of the design process
  7. Ability to advise design teams and advocate for performance goals with clients
  8. Strong verbal and written communication skills
  9. Capacity to ask questions, draw out insight, and synthesize ideas
  10. Eagerness to learn and share new methods and skills

We’ll give additional consideration to candidates with:

  1. Professional licensure or credentials (RA, PE, LEED AP, LFA, CPHC, WELL AP, and/or BEMP)
  2. Proficiency in or desire to learn scripting for analysis automation
  3. Experience with or eagerness to explore applied AI workflows (LLM-assisted research and synthesis, automated reporting, and AI-assisted coding)
  4. Familiarity with post-occupancy evaluation, measurement and verification, and building operations data
  5. Working knowledge of material health, environmental product declarations, and whole-building life cycle assessment

Working Here

We offer a competitive salary and a comprehensive benefits package that includes paid time off and paid holidays; a medical and prescription plan with an employer-funded health reimbursement arrangement; dental and vision care coverage; short and long term disability and life insurance; and paid family leave. Our retirement package includes a 401(k) plan with employer contribution and an employee stock ownership plan (ESOP). We work out of our Philadelphia studio, with a policy that provides for one remote day per week.

How to Apply

Please submit the following via our website by clicking here:

  1. A cover letter indicating your interest in the position
  2. A current resume including three references
  3. A project portfolio or work samples


Please note that hyperlinks to websites or portfolios are considered supplementary and may not be reviewed.

Due to the volume of interested applicants, we are unable to respond to telephone inquiries. Recruiter submissions will not be accepted.

KieranTimberlake is an Equal Opportunity and Affirmative Action employer committed to a workplace free from unlawful discrimination and harassment. Protected veterans and individuals with disabilities are encouraged to apply. If you are a qualified individual with a disability or a disabled veteran and require reasonable accommodation to apply, please contact Human Resources at hrmanager @ kierantimberlake. com.

posting.title: Chief Executive Officer
posting.description:
The Organization

The Center for Early Learning Excellence (CELE) is a new non-profit organization that has been many years in the making. Baton Rouge has the opportunity to become a city where every child has the foundational experiences before kindergarten that ensure a strong start and help them thrive throughout their lives. The founding CEO of the Center for Early Learning Excellence will help make this happen. CELE’s mission is to prepare young children for success and transform the future of the Greater Baton Rouge area by fostering and investing in a thriving early learning ecosystem that continually improves outcomes.


The organization was created by a diverse group of community leaders, including families, providers, educators, advocates, philanthropists, and policymakers, following more than three years of planning and community engagement to identify opportunities to improve early childhood education and chart a path toward a stronger early childhood ecosystem.


The early years of a child’s life shape everything that comes after. Yet, in Baton Rouge, too many families face barriers when trying to access high-quality early care and education (ECE). Fragmented systems, inconsistent communication, limited investments, and limited capacity across 200+ providers make it hard for children, families, and early learning providers to thrive. Over 15,000 children under age five in East Baton Rouge parish do not have access to a high-quality early childhood education their families can afford. Assessments show half of children in the parish enter kindergarten not ready to learn. Meanwhile, available public funding programs and many high-quality early learning providers have long waiting lists. These challenges along with key organizations, assets, and opportunities have been documented with additional details in recent years by the East Baton Rouge Ready Start Network, the Baton Rouge Area Foundation, the Founding Committee, the Louisiana Policy Institute for Children, and others.


CELE will be the hub that connects early childhood programs, aligns funding and policy, builds shared infrastructure, and helps families access the childcare they need. The organization will work to:

  1. Strengthen understanding of the importance of ECE across the community;
  2. Grow investment in ECE to improve both access and quality;
  3. Increase the number of children who are prepared for kindergarten;
  4. Improve accessibility and coordinated enrollment for families to access ECE programs that work for them; and
  5. Better connect systems and institutions to support young children and their families.


The Center for Early Learning Excellence will lead the charge in transforming early care and education in Baton Rouge and building a sustainable, community-driven system that prioritizes families and children.


About the Role

We are seeking an entrepreneurial leader who is strategic, relationship-oriented, and dynamic to serve as the founding CEO of the Center for Early Learning Excellence. The CEO will lead the development and implementation of a bold strategic plan to strengthen the early childhood education system across Baton Rouge. The Center for Early Learning Excellence’s founding CEO will guide a growing team, build and sustain strong partnerships with local providers, government agencies, funders, and families, and drive systemic improvements that expand access, improve quality, and support the ECE workforce. The CEO will spearhead efforts to design and implement a more aligned, accessible, and high-quality early childhood system that meets the needs of all children and families in Baton Rouge. The CEO reports directly to the Board of Directors and manages all day-to-day operations while the Board of Directors executes governance responsibilities.


Key Responsibilities

The CEO will be responsible for leading a team of employees and contractors to execute on:


System Leadership

  1. Serve as the organization's strategic lead, setting a clear vision, defining priorities, and aligning partners to strengthen the ECE system across Baton Rouge.
  2. Lead the development and continuous refinement of a comprehensive strategic plan focused on expanding access, improving quality, and supporting the ECE workforce.
  3. Work with partners to ensure effective implementation of a community-wide ECE strategic plan.
  4. Define a clear, shared vision of ECE quality that includes provider support and a strong focus on workforce development.
  5. Identify system gaps and roles and responsibilities the Center for Early Learning Excellence should address to best fulfill its mission.
  6. Stay informed of local, regional, and national best practices to ensure the ECE system remains responsive to local context and evolving conditions.


Funding Strategy

  1. Serving as the chief fundraiser for the organization and the ECE system in Baton Rouge, in partnership with the Board of Directors and others.
  2. Lead private sector fundraising to fuel growth of existing high-quality programs and to fund new opportunities and partnerships to advance a holistic thriving ECE ecosystem for young children and families from birth to five.
  3. Develop and implement a strategy to maximize every philanthropic and public dollar to provide quality care and education to as many children as possible in the mixed delivery early childhood system through pilots and partnerships, ensuring high-quality service delivery, and supporting participating providers and families.
  4. Oversee strategic financing efforts, including efforts to increase sustainable philanthropic and public funding for ECE in Baton Rouge and support sustainable growth of the organization and the region’s early learning system.


Partnerships

  1. Build and maintain strong, collaborative relationships with all ECE providers, including public schools, private centers, Head Start grantees, and family child care providers, as well as health care providers, and other organizations and agencies that provide services to families with young children.
  2. Build and sustain a coalition of public and private partners, including ECE providers, business, government agencies, community leaders, and funders, who can act through influence, funding, and leadership to implement the community-wide plan.
  3. Pursue Louisiana Department of Education Ready Start designation and transition responsibilities smoothly from the local school system, ensuring appropriate approvals by all parties.
  4. Serve as a visible, trusted spokesperson and advocate for the local ECE system.


Communications

  1. Develop and lead a family-centered communications strategy to ensure families can easily navigate the system and access available services.
  2. Build a strong brand among the Baton Rouge community to invest in the entire community’s ECE vision and plan.
  3. Tell the story of ECE in Baton Rouge in ways that are compelling and attract resources and support to advance collective efforts to strengthen the local ECE system.
  4. Advocate with policy makers and others to bring additional resources to the ECE system.


Organizational Development

  1. Lead organization startup and launch, and support its scaling and long-term sustainability, including hiring staff, securing resources, and establishing internal operations.
  2. Support the organization through the development of a multi-year strategic plan in the first year.
  3. Lead a team that ensures the availability of consistent and reliable data to[1] inform planning, drive quality improvement, and measure progress against established goals.
  4. Work closely with the Board of Directors to shape organizational governance and advance the organization’s mission.
  5. Establish systems for effective and transparent financial management and manage budgets, contracts, funding streams, and reporting requirements.
  6. Ensure compliance with local, state, and federal laws and requirements, and report transparently to stakeholders.
  7. Other duties as assigned.


Qualifications and Experience

Required Experience

  1. Bachelor’s degree in education, public policy, public administration, nonprofit management, or a related field.
  2. Proven leadership experience in early childhood education, education systems and nonprofits or public-sector organizations.
  3. Understanding of ECE systems, programs, regulations, and funding sources (e.g., Head Start, Child Care Assistance Program, etc.).
  4. Experience leading cross-sector initiatives and building partnerships across diverse stakeholders.
  5. Demonstrated success in fundraising, grant management, and public-private partnerships.
  6. Track record of launching or scaling initiatives, especially in early childhood or human services.


Preferred Experience

  1. Advanced degree (e.g., M.Ed., MPA, MBA, MSW, JD, or a related field).
  2. Knowledge of Baton Rouge communities
  3. Deep knowledge of the local, statewide, regional and national ECE landscape
  4. Experience with strategic financing and resource development to support system-wide initiatives
  5. Experience working directly with families, community organizations, and/or government agencies to strengthen access to early childhood or human services.


Skills and Characteristics

  1. Entrepreneurial strategic thinker with an operational lens: you see the big picture AND execute the details
  2. Relationship builder who can earn trust across institutions and communities
  3. Clear communicator who can make complex systems understandable to families, funders, and policymakers
  4. Comfortable with ambiguity, adaptable, and energized by building something from scratch
  5. Deep commitment to supporting young children and families in Baton Rouge


Role Logistics

  1. Anticipated Start Date: January 2027
  2. Salary Range: $150,000 - $175,000/year
  3. Benefits: To be finalized in consultation with selected candidate, but expected to include health, dental, and vision insurance; retirement; paid time off; and a budget for professional development.
  4. Travel: Must have access to reliable transportation and the ability to travel locally around the Baton Rouge area
  5. Reports To: Board of Directors
  6. Application Deadline: Applications will be accepted and reviewed on a rolling basis through 3 pm CT Monday, November 2, 2026

posting.title: Climate Corps Fellow - Summer 2027
posting.description:
EDF Climate Corps Fellow

Environmental Defense Fund

Multiple locations, including New York, NY; San Francisco, CA; Chicago, IL; Boston, MA; and other U.S. cities and towns.

Remote, hybrid, and on-site options available.

Job Type: 10-12 week summer fellowship

Are you a graduate student ready to make a real difference in the fight against climate change? We are looking for graduate students from a wide range of backgrounds who are motivated to join the climate workforce. EDF Climate Corps fellows work with companies, public institutions, and non-profits to identify opportunities to reduce emissions and drive sustainable change across their operations and supply chains.

Fellows are matched with host organizations based on interests, skills, and host needs. You can view the full list of past organizations on our website. A list of 2027 host organizations will be available to well-qualified applicants. We prioritize projects that work on:

  1. Climate commitments and roadmaps
  2. Climate risk
  3. Climate-smart food and ag systems
  4. Environmental and climate justice
  5. Renewables and energy efficiency
  6. Supplier engagement and Scope 3
  7. Sustainable finance
  8. Zero-emission vehicles and fleet transition

EDF Climate Corps provides…

Hands-on Impact: We prioritize projects with clear and actionable goals, so you have the biggest impact possible. We’ve placed over 2,000 fellows in organizations like Citizens Bank, Google, Colgate-Palmolive, McCain Foods, and Ulta Beauty.

Career Development: Before you begin, you will attend Foundations Week- a week of professional development to equip you with the tools you’ll need for a successful fellowship and for your career as a climate professional. Throughout the summer, you’ll receive continuous cohort-based support from subject matter experts, Climate Corps staff, and peers. After your fellowship, you will have access to continuing education and career support.

Network Building: You will have the opportunity to build connections through regional events, online community, and mentorship.

You’ll be a great fellow if you are….

• Enrolled in a graduate certificate or degree program for at least one term of the 2026-2027 academic year [required]

  1. Eligible to work in the United States during the summer of 2027 [required]
  2. Able to participate Foundations Week, the approximately 40-hour week of learning and networking in late May [required]

• A self-starter with project management, leadership skills, and a proven ability to align and collaborate across teams

• Able to present ideas and engage in discussions with stakeholders across all levels of an organization

  1. Comfortable using data to solve problems
  2. Have a passion for solving environmental challenges to build a vital earth for everyone

Depending on the available projects, skills in financial analysis, greenhouse gas accounting, and reporting frameworks are valuable assets.

Please note that our projects require a variety of talents, and we're looking for fellows from a wide range of fields. As Climate Corps aims to strengthen the next generation of climate leaders to accelerate the transition to a clean energy future for all, we recognize that our individual and collective futures depend on the contributions of people from all backgrounds and identities to create lasting environmental solutions. We are proud of the diversity of our fellow cohorts and believes this makes our program stronger.

Compensation

A minimum of $1,400 per week for 10-12 weeks, plus $1,400 for participation in Foundations Week. Compensation and relocation support vary by host organization and will be disclosed to qualified applicants in the project selection process.

Application Deadline

Please visit our website to complete your 2027 fellow application. The application deadline is December 20, 2026 11:59 pm PT. For more information about the timeline and program, please visit the Climate Corps website.

Questions? Please email our team at EDFClimateCorps.apply@edf.org.

Want to learn more about our program? Stay up to date!
